rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4 and Tables 3-5 report the authors' own training and testing of a modified MobileNetV2 (depthwise CNN with SE blocks and residual skip connections) on the PlantVillage leaf-image dataset (Mohanty et al., 2016), with accuracy 0.98 and F1 0.98 on a held-out test split, plus an ablation study.
rows.notes: The study is a primary deep-learning classification experiment, but it does not provide evidence for the claim. The technology is not remote sensing: the model is trained and tested on close-up RGB images of individual leaves from the public PlantVillage dataset and on random online images, not on UAV or satellite imagery (Section 3.1, Figure 1, Figure 6). The effect is not the claimed one: the model classifies leaves into 38 disease/healthy classes (Table 4); it does not grade infection severity, does not detect disease before canopy-wide symptoms (images already show visible leaf symptoms), and does not test or measure any targeted response or pest-control outcome. Statements about enabling early intervention and crop protection (Section 4.3, Conclusions) are assertions, not results. At most the study supports a precondition (image-based detection) of the claimed effect. Limitations mentioned (data imbalance, interpretability) and dispersion measures are not reported for the claimed effect since the claim itself is not tested.

notes: Full text appears complete. Note the abstract and Discussion report 98% accuracy while the Conclusions state 96%, an internal inconsistency; irrelevant to the claim rating since Q2 is no.
